sections.body:
### What is congregate care?

"Congregate care" is the state's term for places where kids live in a group, away from home, with staff in charge around the clock. Under Utah law, four kinds of programs count as congregate care when they serve kids ([Utah Code 26B-2-101](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title26B/Chapter2/26B-2-S101.html), subsection 13). It's the same list [SB 127](https://le.utah.gov/~2021/bills/sbillenr/SB0127.htm) used in 2021:

- **Outdoor youth programs:** a "24-hour outdoor group living environment," including wilderness therapy and adventure therapy
- **Residential treatment programs:** a "24-hour group living environment" offering treatment, "behavior modification" or "discipline," including locked intermediate secure treatment
- **Therapeutic schools:** live-in schools for kids with "a history of failing to function" at home or in school
- **Residential support programs:** supervised group living for people who need care or protection

### How this connects to the troubled teen industry

The wilderness programs, residential treatment centers and therapeutic boarding schools that make up the troubled teen industry are, in Utah's legal language, congregate care. So when Utah writes congregate care law, it is writing the rules for the TTI programs inside its borders.

Survivors pushed for that law. In February 2021, Paris Hilton, who was sent to Provo Canyon School as a teen, testified for SB 127, sponsored by Sen. Mike McKell ([Deseret News](https://www.deseret.com/utah/2021/2/8/22272722/paris-hilton-testifies-in-support-of-bill-to-regulate-troubled-teen-centers-provo-legislature-2021/)). It wrote limits on restraint and seclusion in these programs into state law; they are now in [Utah Code 26B-2-123](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title26B/Chapter2/26B-2-S123.html). In 2025, McKell's SB 297 created the state's Congregate Care Advisory Committee, which meets in public and takes public comment, so survivors can attend and speak.
